prediction.text:
In its fiscal 2025 10-K risk factors, NVIDIA said U.S. export controls and licensing for China-bound products are uncertain and could hurt its business. It said the rules can change at any time, and the licensing process is closed and unpredictable. It also said the rules put NVIDIA at a competitive disadvantage and could effectively exclude it from all or part of the China market. It said excessive or shifting controls could also reduce demand in other markets and push customers to alternatives.
NVIDIA warned that the U.S. government has changed, and may again change, the export control rules at any time. That could subject a wider range of its products to export restrictions and licensing requirements, negatively affecting its business and financial results. The filing also says this could effectively exclude NVIDIA from all or part of the China market.
On licensing, NVIDIA said it has no assurance the U.S. government will grant a license or act on an application in a timely manner or at all. It described the government's review as a closed process without clear standards or an opportunity for review.
NVIDIA said the requirements have a disproportionate impact on it and have already disadvantaged, and may in the future disadvantage, NVIDIA against competitors.
NVIDIA said excessive or shifting export controls may reduce demand for its products and services not only in China but also in other markets such as Europe, Latin America and Southeast Asia. It said they have already encouraged, and may in the future encourage, customers outside China and other impacted regions to "design-out" certain U.S. semiconductors.
NVIDIA also said licensing requirements encourage customers in China to pursue alternatives to its products.

caveats: The summary is based on Item 1A of the fiscal 2025 10-K (fiscal year ended January 26, 2025). It uses only the verified quotes from three passages.

Two other relevant passages were seen only as search snippets and were not verified, so they are not relied on. One covers licensing for China shipments and the other covers the 2023 U.S. restrictions on China.
